candidates.tagline: FIFA declared ketchup a branding threat and taped it into witness protection
candidates.story: FIFA's 2026 World Cup 'clean stadium' rules required workers to apply black tape over every non-sponsor condiment label in the venues — turning rows of ketchup, mustard, hot sauce and BBQ bottles into redacted documents; Heinz responded by releasing a limited 'Unofficial Stadium Ketchup' with the label intentionally blacked out.
candidates.why_funny: It takes a special kind of corporate overreach to make a bottle of ketchup feel like classified intelligence.
candidates.alt: A condiment station with rows of ketchup, mustard, hot sauce, BBQ sauce and soy sauce bottles lined up on a red counter, most with wide black tape strips covering their brand labels

candidates.tagline: Sony spent 6 years selling disc-drive consoles. Now ending all game discs.
candidates.story: Sony announced on July 1, 2026 that physical disc production for all new PlayStation games will end in January 2028 — simultaneously with GTA 6 confirming that its $80 'physical edition' ships with only a download code in an empty cardboard box, with no disc ever planned.
candidates.why_funny: They engineered a beautifully slotted disc drive into millions of consoles, then announced the slot is now purely decorative.
candidates.alt: A PlayStation 5 disc-edition console displayed in a locked glass case at a Japanese electronics store, with the Sony logo and PlayStation 5 branding visible
